principles: Lattice remains the authority layer; hosts are execution surfaces only.
Manual handoff and local receipt evidence must work before supervised dispatch is trusted.
Every overflow task must be bounded by scope, base/head identity, commands, and a receipt.
Unavailable Claude Code must produce actionable diagnostics, not a broken workflow.
No command may imply productionDone or verified receipt without server authority verification.
drivers: Codex agent scarcity requires bounded parallelism without losing state integrity.
Existing handoff/host surfaces should be extended rather than replaced.
Review/TEST/DONE gates need mechanical evidence, not chat-only claims.

options.name: extend-existing-handoff
pros: Can preserve backward compatibility with handoff-pack-v0
cons: Requires carefully distinguishing generic handoff from overflow receipt semantics

options.name: new-overflow-subsystem
pros: Could model every future host workflow independently
cons: Higher risk of command sprawl and confused authority boundary

options.name: supervised-runner-first
pros: Could reduce manual operator steps when Claude Code is installed
cons: Risks overclaiming external host results before receipt/scope gates are solid

rationale: Extending existing handoff surfaces gives the user a practical overflow path while preserving the proven no-overclaim authority boundary and avoiding a premature runner.

preMortem.scenario: Claude Code unavailable is treated as failure of Lattice itself
preMortem.trigger: host_dispatch tries to execute a missing claude binary
preMortem.consequence: Users lose trust and local story workflow appears blocked
preMortem.mitigation: Make host availability diagnostic-only with status unavailable/warn and nextAction; no local gate is blocked by missing Claude Code.

preMortem.scenario: External host output is trusted without scope or receipt
preMortem.trigger: Receipt submit accepts changed files outside allowedPaths or stale base/head
preMortem.consequence: Codex may merge unreviewed or out-of-scope changes
preMortem.mitigation: Receipt submit computes scopeStatus and freshness, stores local accepted/rejected state, and keeps productionDone=false until verified authority exists.

preMortem.scenario: Handoff pack relies on hidden Codex context
preMortem.trigger: Pack omits objective, commands, success criteria, or denied paths
preMortem.consequence: Claude Code cannot safely execute the task or returns unverifiable prose
preMortem.mitigation: Pack schema includes objective, role, allowed/denied paths, required commands, success criteria, baseSha, packHash, and explicit instructions not to edit story JSON.

preMortem.scenario: Supervised dispatch becomes a secret agent runner
preMortem.trigger: host_dispatch starts trying to manage vendor runtime deeply
preMortem.consequence: Lattice violates host-neutral boundaries and duplicates Codex/Claude behavior
preMortem.mitigation: First release is projection/dry-run oriented, records planned metadata, and never auto-trusts or auto-merges results.
